page: Amazon Web Services m7i.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data positions the m7i.2xlarge primarily in the average performance tier for general-purpose workloads. It demonstrates strong performance in text processing, scoring 2359.0 in Geekbench text processing tests, which falls into the top 25% tier. In standard compute benchmarks, it achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1790.0 and a multi-core score of 6809.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 579.72 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and approximately 50.51 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

While the instance features advanced CPU instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, its performance on larger models is limited by the lack of a dedicated GPU. For example, LLM inference text generation using a medium 7B model is relatively weak at 7.71 tokens per second, placing it in the bottom 25%. However, it handles smaller 135M models more efficiently, processing prompts at 1017.23 tokens per second. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for general-purpose workloads, web serving, Redis databases, and text processing tasks that benefit from modern DDR5 memory and dedicated CPU allocation without requiring local NVMe storage.
